flawed_step: Step 4: Inferring that two minimum spanning trees must have the same edge set. Equal minimum weight does not imply uniqueness.
counterexample: Let the graph be the triangle on vertices a,b,c, with all three edges ab, ac, bc having weight 1. A legal Kruskal run selects ab and then bc, producing {ab,bc}. A legal Prim run starting at a selects ac and then bc, producing {ac,bc}. These distinct edge sets are both minimum spanning trees.
assessment_summary:
1. Fix an arbitrary connected weighted graph G and arbitrary legal runs of Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms on G. — JUSTIFIED: This is the correct setup for attempting to prove the universal claim.
2. Kruskal's output is a minimum spanning tree of G. — JUSTIFIED: This is the standard correctness property of Kruskal's algorithm, including arbitrary legal tie-breaking.
3. Prim's output is a minimum spanning tree of G. — JUSTIFIED: This is the standard correctness property of Prim's algorithm, independent of the start vertex and legal tie-breaking.
4. Since both outputs are minimum spanning trees, they have the same edge set. — NOT JUSTIFIED: Minimum spanning trees have the same total weight, but need not have the same edges unless the MST is unique; the hypotheses do not ensure uniqueness.
5. Therefore every legal Kruskal run and every legal Prim run output the same tree. — NOT JUSTIFIED: This conclusion depends on the invalid uniqueness inference in Step 4.
6. To test that failed inference, take the connected triangle with vertices a,b,c and give every edge weight 1. — JUSTIFIED: This is a connected weighted graph allowed by the definitions.
7. Kruskal may break ties by considering ab first and bc second, accepting both and outputting {ab,bc}. — JUSTIFIED: Both edges have minimum available weight and do not form a cycle when accepted.
8. Prim may start at a, select ac first, and then select bc, outputting {ac,bc}. — JUSTIFIED: At each stage the selected edge is a minimum-weight edge crossing from the current tree to an unvisited vertex; ties are unrestricted.
9. The two outputs have different edge sets. — JUSTIFIED: The Kruskal tree contains ab but not ac, while the Prim tree contains ac but not ab.
10. Both outputs are minimum spanning trees. — JUSTIFIED: Each is a spanning tree with two weight-1 edges and total weight 2; every spanning tree on three vertices has two edges, all of weight 1, so no lower total weight is possible.
11. Hence the asserted universal equality of outputs is false. — JUSTIFIED: Steps 6–10 give two legal runs on the same graph whose minimum spanning trees have different edge sets.
